description.narrative: The project will provide additional new and rehabilitated water supply infrastructure and extend system coverage to expand access to safe water in nine towns. The project will also provide piped water supply to an additional 58,000 residents through (i) a new water supply system in Stung Treng, (ii) a new distribution zone in Siem Reap, and (iii) system expansion in Kampong Cham and Svay Rieng. In addition, the project will rehabilitate existing water treatment plants in seven towns. The project interventions will replicate initiatives that made PPWSA successful and build on PPWSA experience. It will also incorporate lessons from previous ADB projects. The project will help the PWW's reduce real NRW levels to below 15% by using improved material and construction practices in its works to complement ongoing NRW reduction initiatives by the service providers and other development partners.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved water supply infrastructure and service provision in selected provincial waterworks.

Through about 438 km of new pipelines the urban population served in Kampong Cham, Siem Reap, Stung Treng, and Svay Rieng will be increased by more than 11,600 households (approx. 58,000 people of whom 51% or 29,280 are women), with equal access to all households and subsidies of up to 100% for connections for the poor. Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: Achieved by approx. 50%. Data Source: Annual reports by provincial waterworks and MIH; project progress reports; project completion report.

Real NRW levels reduced to less than 15% for all participating water utilities. Achievement: n.a. Progress/Status: No actual data was submitted on achievement of the indicator. However, the EA has committed to set up an additional package to improve NRW management and supply required equipment and Knowhow under the loan extension. Data Source: Annual reports by provincial waterworks and MIH; project progress reports; project completion report. Actual value: n.a.

All project stakeholders including water end users, poor households, affected peoples and civil society organizations are fully consulted through public and household consultations and the media. Approximately 275,000 women and girls will receive improve water supply services across the nine project towns. Progress/Status: Consultations with water end users, poor households, affected peoples and others have taken place, regular monitoring and reporting documented in the SESMRs. Connection of additional households with increased access to safe water supply for women and girls ongoing. Data Source: Annual reports by provincial waterworks and MIH; project progress reports; project completion report. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

MIH implements corporate principles at public waterworks and provides them with full financial autonomy. Achievement: ongoing Progress/Status: The implementation process is ongoing and shall be implemented latest by end of extended loan closure in December 2022. Data Source: Annual reports by provincial waterworks and MIH; project progress reports; project completion report. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N

Standard system of regulation and tariff setting based on customer affordability and full-cost recovery adopted for participating waterworks. Achievement: ongoing Progress/Status: The implementation process is ongoing and shall be complied with latest by end of extended loan closure in December 2022. Data Source: Annual reports by provincial waterworks and MIH; project progress reports; project completion report. Base year: 2014 Baseline value: N
